description: Capture page -- a dev-only interaction recording tool available exclusively in the runner application. Users record mouse and keyboard interactions along with screen video to create data for State Machine construction from desktop and mixed-environment workflows. The tool captures input events as timestamped JSONL data synchronized with video frames, enabling analysis of complex multi-step user interactions including drag operations and cross-application workflows.

groups.name: Recording Controls and Session Management
groups.description: The core recording workflow is straightforward: users click Start Recording to begin capturing, then Stop Recording to end the session. While recording, a live timer shows elapsed duration with a pulsing red indicator, and an event counter tracks the number of mouse and keyboard events captured. The recording captures three types of data simultaneously: mouse input, keyboard input, and screen video. Users configure the video FPS before starting. The start and stop buttons provide clear visual feedback about the current state and disable appropriately to prevent double-starts or premature stops.

assertions.description: Users can start an interaction recording session by clicking a prominently displayed Start Recording button, which begins capturing mouse, keyboard, and video data simultaneously
Users see indicators for the three captured input types -- Mouse, Keyboard, and Video -- so they understand the scope of data being recorded
Users see a clear header identifying this as the Interaction Recording tool, with a subtitle explaining it captures input for State Machine creation
Users see explanatory text describing the purpose of recording interactions -- to create State Machines from complex workflows, drags, and multi-step processes

groups.name: Recording Settings
groups.description: Before starting a recording, users can configure capture settings through a collapsible settings panel. The primary setting is video FPS, which controls the frame rate of screen recording and can be adjusted between 10 and 60 FPS using a slider. Higher FPS produces smoother video but larger files, with 30 FPS recommended as the default. Settings are disabled during an active recording to prevent mid-session configuration changes that could corrupt data.

assertions.description: Users can open and close a settings panel to configure recording parameters before starting a session, keeping the main interface uncluttered
Users can adjust the video capture frame rate using an FPS slider, balancing between smoother video quality and smaller file sizes
Users see guidance that higher FPS gives smoother video but larger files, with 30 FPS recommended as the default, helping them make informed configuration choices

groups.name: Recording Output and Results
groups.description: After stopping a recording, users see a summary of the captured session including duration and total event count. The last recording section persists until a new recording is started, allowing users to review and access the output files. Users can open the output folder containing the JSONL events file and video recording directly from the interface. This output data serves as input for creating State Machines that model complex user interaction patterns.

assertions.description: The info section explains the purpose (State Machine creation), output format (JSONL events with timestamps), and use cases (drag operations, multi-step workflows, desktop app automation)
Users understand that recordings produce input events in JSONL format with timestamps that can be correlated with video frames for analysis
Users see documented use cases for recordings including complex drag operations, multi-step workflows, and desktop app automation, helping them understand when to use this tool

states.name: Idle — Ready to Record
states.description: The initial state of the Capture page. The user sees the page header, input type indicators (Mouse, Keyboard, Video), a description of the tool's purpose, and a green Start Recording button. No recording is active and no previous recording results are displayed.

states.name: Recording in Progress
states.description: An active recording session is underway. A pulsing red indicator and live timer show elapsed duration. An event counter displays the number of captured mouse and keyboard events. A red Stop Recording button is prominently displayed. The Start Recording button is not visible.

states.name: Recording Completed — Results Available
states.description: A recording session has finished. The user sees the Start Recording button again (ready for another session) plus a Last Recording summary section showing session duration, event count, and an Open Output Folder link to access the JSONL events file and video.

states.name: Settings Panel Expanded
states.description: The collapsible settings panel is open, showing the Video FPS slider (range 10-60, default 30) and a recommendation note. The slider is disabled during an active recording. This state overlays either idle or completed.

states.name: Error Banner Displayed
states.description: An error occurred while starting or stopping a recording. A red error banner with an AlertCircle icon is displayed at the top of the main content area, showing the error message. This state overlays the current base state (idle or completed). The error clears when the user retries the action.
